要去做一场躲不掉的对话

en.meditation:
This was said to someone standing at the edge of something he had never done, following a leader nobody could replace. And God's answer is not a strategy. It is a presence — wherever you go, which is the part that covers the places you have not thought of yet.

So take it as said to you. The courage you are looking for is not a personality you have to develop first. It is the direct result of who is going with you into today.
en.action_step: Name the one thing today you would rather avoid. Say when it is, out loud, and ask God to go into it with you.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that You go with me into the actual day, not a safer version of it. There are parts of it I am uneasy about, and You have not scolded me for that. Answer the fear with Your presence, and go ahead of me into the thing I am dreading. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Let everything that has breath praise the LORD. Praise the LORD.

traditional.text: Let every thing that hath breath praise the Lord. Praise ye the Lord.

modern.text: Let everything that has breath praise the LORD. Praise the LORD.

exegesis.context_note: This is the last sentence of the entire book of Psalms, which contains far more lament than praise. Read against the 149 psalms before it — including the ones that end in darkness — the qualification it names is deliberately minimal: breath. Nothing else is required.
exegesis.version_note: 本节是诗篇全书的末句;KJV 与 NIV 都保留结尾重复的「哈利路亚」,是整卷书的收束。
life_connection: 觉得自己状态不好不配赞美

en.meditation:
This is the last line of the whole book, and the book it closes contains more complaining than praising. Which makes the qualification worth noticing. Not: let everyone who is doing well praise Him. Let everything that has breath.

So the bar this morning is breathing. Are you? Then you are inside the verse, whatever kind of week this has been.
en.action_step: Take one deliberate breath and say one true good thing about God. That is the whole assignment.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I am not in a good state this morning and I have very little to bring. I am breathing, which You seem to think is enough. So: You are good, and I am saying it. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Worship the LORD your God, and his blessing will be on your food and water. I will take away sickness from among you,

traditional.text: And ye shall serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread, and thy water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of thee.

modern.text: Worship the LORD your God, and his blessing will be on your food and water. I will take away sickness from among you,

exegesis.context_note: This is covenant language given to Israel at Sinai, not a general health guarantee — the promises are tied to a specific people and a specific agreement. What is striking is the scale of what gets blessed: not visions or victories, but bread and water. The most ordinary things on the table.
key_themes: 最普通的东西也被看顾
exegesis.version_note: 本节是西奈之约中对以色列的条款,不宜读成对个人健康的普遍保证;和合本作「他必赐福与你的粮与你的水」。
life_connection: 觉得属灵和厨房是两件事
把日常当成不属灵的部分

en.meditation:
Look at what God says He will bless. Not your calling, not your ministry. Your bread and your water.

As Christians we can develop a strange hierarchy where the kitchen is where real life gets interrupted and the quiet time is where it happens. This verse puts the blessing exactly where you spend most of your day. On the food. On the water. On the ordinary.
en.action_step: Say a proper thank you over one ordinary thing today — a meal, a cup of tea, running water.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been treating most of my life as the part that does not count. Bless the ordinary things today — the meals, the washing up, the small provisions I stopped noticing. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Therefore, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Always give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.

traditional.text: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.

modern.text: Therefore, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Always give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.

exegesis.context_note: This is the last line of Paul's chapter on resurrection, and the 'therefore' matters — the argument for not giving up rests entirely on what he has just proved about the dead being raised. The Greek kenos means empty. Paul's claim is that nothing done in Christ ends up hollow.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 not in vain 与 NIV 的 not in vain 同译 kenos「空的」;和合本作「不是徒然的」,三者一致。
life_connection: 带孩子的日子重复而无声

en.meditation:
For about six years I did work that produced nothing I could show anyone. I raised children who do not remember most of it, and held a job where the good parts were invisible. I read this verse then and it annoyed me — it sounded like a pat on the head. What I had missed was one word: therefore. Paul is not offering encouragement. He is drawing a conclusion from a whole chapter about the dead being raised.

Which means it is not a compliment about my effort. It is a claim about where things go. Nothing that goes in ends up empty. I did not feel that then. I have come to believe it since.
en.action_step: Name one long stretch of work that produced nothing visible. Say out loud that it was not empty.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have spent years on things nobody can see and I have quietly wondered whether any of it landed anywhere. Thank You that nothing done in You ends up hollow. I cannot see where it went. I am going to trust that You can. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says.

traditional.text: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.

modern.text: Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says.

exegesis.context_note: The Greek paralogizomai is an accounting word: to miscalculate, to reckon something into your account that is not there. James is not scolding people for weak effort — he is naming a specific self-deception, where hearing something gets recorded as having done it.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 deceiving your own selves 与 NIV 的 deceive yourselves 同译 paralogizomai「用错误的推算骗自己」,是会计用语。

en.meditation:
The word for deceiving is an accounting term: putting something in your account that is not actually there. Which is exactly what happens when a good sermon feels like progress.

James is not asking us for a transformed life by Friday. He is asking for one thing to move from the hearing column into the doing column. One. Today. Let's each pick ours.
en.action_step: Take one thing you have known you should do for weeks and do it today, badly if necessary.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been crediting myself for things I only understood. Move one of them across today. Show me which, and let me do it before I have finished thinking about it. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own;

traditional.text: What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?

modern.text: Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own;

exegesis.context_note: Paul wrote this to a church tolerating sexual exploitation, so the original target is specific. But the claim underneath is broader than its first application: the body is not a lesser part of a person, and it is not a problem to be overcome. It is where God has chosen to live.
key_themes: 身体不是需要克服的东西
不属自己是安全不是控制
exegesis.version_note: 本节原文是针对当时的淫乱问题;今日常被用于健康与自我形象,应用可以,但须知其原始语境。
life_connection: 长年对自己的身体不满意
只在身体出问题时才注意它

en.meditation:
Most of us have a long and unkind relationship with our own body. It has been the thing to fix, to hide, to push through, to apologise for. Very few women reach forty without a running critique playing somewhere underneath.

Paul cuts under all of it with one claim. This is where God chose to live. Not the version of it you had ten years ago, and not the version you keep promising to get back to. This one, this morning, with everything it has carried and everything it can no longer do as easily. He moved in. He has not asked for a different one!
en.action_step: Do one thing today that treats your body kindly — food, water, sleep, or stopping when it says to.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been unkind about my body for most of my life, and I have called that discipline. You chose to live here. Teach me to treat it the way You do — not as a project, and not as a disappointment. Show me one kind thing to do for it today. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified because of them, for the LORD your God goes with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you.

traditional.text: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.

modern.text: Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified because of them, for the LORD your God goes with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you.

exegesis.context_note: Moses says this to the whole nation before repeating it privately to Joshua — the courage is not reserved for leaders. 'Because of them' points at specific opponents rather than a general anxiety. The double negative in Hebrew is emphatic: not fail, not forsake.
key_themes: 说给全会众不只给领袖
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee 是希伯来的双重否定强调;和合本作「必不撇下你,也不丢弃你」。

en.meditation:
Notice this is said to everyone first, and only afterwards to Joshua on his own. Courage is not issued only to the person in charge.

And notice how specific it is: do not be afraid because of them. Not a general instruction about anxiety — a particular set of people, on a particular day. As Christians we can spiritualise fear into something vague. Scripture usually keeps it concrete, because that is where it actually lives.
en.action_step: Name the specific person or meeting you are dreading. Pray about that one, by name.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, it is not fear in general this morning. It is one particular conversation and one particular person. Go with me into that room. Thank You that You will not fail me and will not walk out. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: So in Christ Jesus you are all children of God through faith,

traditional.text: For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.

modern.text: So in Christ Jesus you are all children of God through faith,

exegesis.context_note: Paul is arguing against a church being told they needed extra credentials to properly belong. In that world, status was everything — and 'all' is the sharp word in the sentence. Sonship here is a legal term: full standing in a household, including inheritance, not affectionate language.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 children of God 与 NIV 同;下一节的洗礼语境说明这是身份的宣告,不是奖赏。

en.meditation:
Notice the word all. Paul is writing to people who were being told they needed extra credentials to properly belong. Which is still the water most of us swim in. Ask a woman who she is and she will usually tell you what she does, and if that has recently changed — a job lost, a role ended, children grown — she will hesitate before answering.

This verse hands you a standing that no promotion ever granted and no redundancy letter can revoke, because neither of them issued it. You are a child of God, through faith, this morning, before you have produced one single thing today!
en.action_step: Introduce yourself to yourself this morning without mentioning your job or your role. Say what remains.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I define myself by what I produce, and on the days I produce nothing I do not know who I am. Thank You that this standing was given and not earned, and cannot be taken back by anyone who did not grant it. Let me work today out of that instead of for it. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.

traditional.text: They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

modern.text: They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.

exegesis.context_note: Jeremiah wrote this from the ruins of Jerusalem, around 586 BC — not from safety but from rubble. The word behind 'faithfulness' is emunah: something firm enough to stand on, not a warm feeling. He is describing what held when everything else fell.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 lovingkindness 与 NIV 的 unfailing love 同指 chesed;「诚实」的希伯来 emunah 本义是稳固、站得住。
life_connection: 对自己的进度失去耐心

en.meditation:
Jeremiah wrote this while his city lay in ruins. Not from comfort — from rubble. And still he counts what is new.

Notice the timing. God's kindness is not stockpiled and rationed to the deserving; it arrives fresh, each morning, whether you slept well or barely slept at all. Yesterday's portion is gone because you no longer need it. What waits for you today was made for today.
en.action_step: Before you reach for your phone, say one sentence out loud: today has its own mercy.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for meeting me at the start of this day rather than at the end of my strength. I woke up still holding yesterday. Help me set it down, and give me eyes for what You made new this morning. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: “ 'The LORD bless you and keep you;

traditional.text: The Lord bless thee, and keep thee:

modern.text: “ 'The LORD bless you and keep you;

exegesis.context_note: God dictates this blessing word for word and tells the priests to say it over the people — the text notes that in doing so they put God's name on them. It is the oldest biblical text ever found, on a small silver scroll from around 600 BC. It was made to be spoken aloud, not read privately.
exegesis.version_note: 本节是亚伦祝福的第一句,原为祭司向全会众宣告之用;和合本作「愿耶和华赐福给你,保护你」。

en.meditation:
God did not describe this blessing. He dictated it, word for word, and told the priests to say it out loud over people. Which means it was always meant to be heard, not read. And most of us are much better at pronouncing blessing over others than receiving any.

So who last said something like this over you? And if the honest answer is nobody in a long time, would you let God say it this morning?
en.action_step: Read the verse aloud with your own name in it. Then say it over one other person today.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I am much better at asking for others than at receiving anything myself. This morning I am going to let You bless me. Bless me and keep me today, and let me pass it on to someone before evening. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,

traditional.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,

modern.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,

exegesis.context_note: The word for fruit is singular in Greek — one fruit with nine aspects, not a checklist of nine. Paul is contrasting this with 'the works of the flesh' in the verses before: works are produced, fruit is grown. Nobody makes an apple by trying harder.
key_themes: 果子是长出来的不是做出来的
exegesis.version_note: 原文的「果子」是单数,九样是同一个果子的九个面,不是九项待办;这是本节最常被误读之处。
life_connection: 拿九样对照自己觉得样样不及格

en.meditation:
Fruit is singular here. One fruit, nine facets — not nine boxes to fail at separately. And notice the contrast Paul is drawing. The list before this one is called works. This one is called fruit. Works are produced; fruit is grown, slowly, by something happening in the plant rather than to it.

Which is why trying harder to be patient has never once made anyone patient. As Christians we can stop straining at the fruit and pay attention to the root instead.
en.action_step: Stop working on the quality you most want to have. Give that time to being with God instead, today.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been trying to manufacture what only You can grow, and then feeling like a failure when it did not appear on schedule. Turn my attention to the root this morning instead of to the fruit. Grow whatever You are growing, at Your own pace, and give me the patience not to keep checking. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: For the LORD gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.

traditional.text: For the Lord giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding.

modern.text: For the LORD gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.

exegesis.context_note: Proverbs 2 begins with a long conditional — if you seek it like silver, if you search for it as for hidden treasure — and then this verse gives the reason the searching works. Wisdom is not extracted by effort; it is given. James 1:5 says the same thing more directly.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 与 NIV 都作「出于他口」;这个意象与雅各书 1:5「求那厚赐与众人的神」相呼应,可同读。
life_connection: 面前有个不知怎么决定的事
觉得聪明人才配有智慧

en.meditation:
The chapter opens with a great deal of searching — seek it like silver, dig for it like treasure. And then this verse explains why any of that works: because the Lord gives it.

So the searching is real, and it is not what produces the wisdom. That comes out of His mouth. Which means the decision in front of you this morning is not a test of how clever you are. Ask for it!
en.action_step: Ask plainly for wisdom about one specific decision. Not guidance in general — that decision.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have a decision in front of me and I have been treating it as a test of my own judgement. You give wisdom. So I am asking, plainly, about this one thing. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Let us then approach God's throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.

traditional.text: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.

modern.text: Let us then approach God's throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.

exegesis.context_note: Hebrews was written to Jewish Christians who knew the holy of holies could be entered once a year, by one man, carrying blood. Against that background, 'come boldly' is startling. The Greek is parrhesia — the freedom of a citizen to speak plainly in public, not the nerve of an intruder.
key_themes: 宝座的名字是恩典不是审查
求助本身就是被允许的
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 come boldly 与 NIV 的 with confidence 同译希腊文 parrhesia;中文和合本作「坦然无惧」。
life_connection: 觉得要先把自己收拾好才配祷告
把神想成会失望的那一位

en.meditation:
As Christians we tend to approach God the way we approach an appraisal — with the case for ourselves already half drafted. Hebrews uses a different word for it: boldly. Not carefully, not once we have tidied ourselves up first.

And notice what the throne is named for. Grace, not review. So let's come as we actually are tonight, and stop rehearsing the explanation on the way in.
en.action_step: Bring God the one thing you were planning to handle by yourself. Say it out loud before you sleep.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I come to You tonight without tidying myself up first, because You said I could. Thank You that this is a throne of grace and not a review. Here is what I need help with, and here is where I fell short. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Go back and tell Hezekiah, the ruler of my people, 'This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears; I will heal you.'

traditional.text: Turn again, and tell Hezekiah the captain of my people, Thus saith the Lord, the God of David thy father, I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will heal thee: on the third day thou shalt go up unto the house of the Lord.

modern.text: Go back and tell Hezekiah, the ruler of my people, 'This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears; I will heal you.'

exegesis.context_note: Hezekiah was terminally ill and had just been told to set his house in order. Isaiah was already leaving the palace when God turned him around. In Hebrew, 'I have seen thy tears' uses the ordinary verb for looking at a thing — no poetic flourish. The point is that God attends to the part of prayer that has no words.
key_themes: 神会收回已经说出的「不」
exegesis.version_note: KJV 与 NIV 都把「听见祷告」与「看见眼泪」并列为两件事,这个并列是本节的解经重心,不可合并。
life_connection: 已经不再向人解释的那件事
哭过之后觉得自己软弱

en.meditation:
Hezekiah had already been told the answer was no; the prophet had walked out. Then God sent him back. And read the order of what God says. Before the promise, before anything changes, there is this: I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears. The tears get their own clause. God does not fold them into the prayer as though weeping were an inefficient way of asking. He counts them separately.

Whatever you have been crying about — the thing you stopped explaining to people because you got tired of explaining it — it has been seen. Not overlooked, not endured. Seen!
en.action_step: Say out loud the thing you have stopped explaining to anyone. You don't have to make a case for it. Just say it.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that You count tears separately from words, and that You have not grown tired of mine. I stopped explaining this to people a while ago. I am not going to stop explaining it to You. Thank You that being seen by You is not the same as being pitied. Hold what I have brought You tonight. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.

traditional.text: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.

modern.text: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.

exegesis.context_note: Paul and Silas had been stripped, beaten with rods and thrown into the innermost cell — Luke is specific about all three. The Greek for their singing, hymneo, is the same verb used of the hymn Jesus sang with his disciples before Gethsemane. That the prisoners 'heard them' is Luke's own detail, and he includes it deliberately.
key_themes: 苦难中的信心从不是全然私人的
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 sang praises 与 NIV 的 singing hymns 同译 hymneo,与耶稣在客西马尼前所唱的是同一个词。
life_connection: 怕自己的情绪影响家人

en.meditation:
Two men, beaten and locked in the inner cell, feet in the stocks. It is midnight. And Luke records what they did with that particular hour: they prayed, and then they sang.

Notice the last clause, because it is the one usually skipped. The other prisoners heard them. Nobody was singing for an audience — there was no audience, only people in the same dark lying awake. But faith in a bad night is never entirely private. The woman in the next room hears. The child down the hall hears. Your midnight is louder than you think, and not always in a bad way.
en.action_step: If you are awake tonight when you would rather be asleep, stop fighting it for ten minutes. Pray in that time instead — out loud, if you can.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I would rather not be awake right now, and I would rather this were over. Thank You that You are not absent from the middle of the night. If I cannot sleep, let me pray. And if anyone near me is listening, let what they hear from me be trust and not despair. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Be completely humble and gentle; be patient, bearing with one another in love.

traditional.text: With all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love;

modern.text: Be completely humble and gentle; be patient, bearing with one another in love.

exegesis.context_note: Paul writes this from prison, opening the practical half of Ephesians. The Greek anechomenoi means to hold up or hold back — the same verb used elsewhere of putting up with hardship. It is not a feeling about people. It is a decision about what you do with the irritation you already have.
key_themes: 最亲近的人最先耗尽耐心
不说出那句有理的重话
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 forbearing one another 与 NIV 的 bearing with one another 同译 anechomenoi,本义是「托住、忍住」。
life_connection: 对家人比对同事更没耐心
一天下来最后一点耐心用在最亲的人身上

en.meditation:
Forbearing is an unglamorous word, and it is the one Paul chooses. Not fixing each other. Not winning the point. Bearing with.

As Christians we sometimes treat patience with people as the lesser virtue — what you settle for when you cannot change them. Paul puts it near the top of the list. Most of the love that actually holds a household or a long friendship together is exactly this: choosing, one more time, not to say the sharp true thing you have every right to say.
en.action_step: Think of the person you were least patient with today. Decide one specific thing you will not bring up tomorrow.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for bearing with me long before I learned to bear with anyone. I confess that my patience runs out fastest with the people closest to me. Grow something slower in me. Where I have every right to say the sharp thing tomorrow, help me choose not to. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Whoever would foster love covers over an offense, but whoever repeats the matter separates close friends.

traditional.text: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.

modern.text: Whoever would foster love covers over an offense, but whoever repeats the matter separates close friends.

exegesis.context_note: Proverbs contrasts two ways of handling someone else's wrong. The Hebrew for 'covereth' is kasah — the same verb used of God covering sin, meaning to put out of sight, not to pretend away. 'Repeateth' is literally to go over something again: the picture of returning to the same ground until a path is worn into it.
key_themes: 沉默要出于爱不是惩罚
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 covereth 与 NIV 的 covers over 同译希伯来 kasah,与神「遮盖罪」用同一个动词。
life_connection: 每次家庭聚会都要重演的那句话
怕放下就等于承认自己错

en.meditation:
Every family has a matter that gets repeated. The thing your mother says every visit. The thing you say back. The old grievance polished so many times it comes out smooth now, almost affectionate, and still does damage. Proverbs is not telling you to pretend it never happened — covering an offence is not the same as denying one. It is deciding that this particular thing has been said enough, and that you will be the one who stops saying it.

So, honestly: which matter in your family have you been repeating? And what would it cost you to let this be the year it goes quiet?
en.action_step: Name the thing you always bring up. Decide now that you will not bring it up next time — and tell God that is your decision, not your defeat.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, there is something I keep repeating, and I have told myself it is honesty. Some of it is. Some of it is just the wound talking. Show me the difference. Give me the strength to let it go quiet without pretending it never hurt, and keep me from turning silence into a weapon. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: The LORD is my shepherd, I lack nothing.

traditional.text: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.

modern.text: The LORD is my shepherd, I lack nothing.

exegesis.context_note: David had actually kept sheep, which is why the picture is unsentimental — shepherding was hard, dirty, night work. The Hebrew behind 'I shall not want' is a single verb meaning to lack. It is not a promise of abundance but of sufficiency: that what is needed will be there.
key_themes: 不缺乏是够用不是丰盛
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 I shall not want 与 NIV 的 I lack nothing 同译一个希伯来动词「缺乏」;和合本作「必不致缺乏」。
life_connection: 睡前清点自己没有的东西
拿别人的生活对比自己的

en.meditation:
Six words, and everything is decided by the first two: the Lord is. Not was, not might be. Present tense, tonight.

And my — David does not say a shepherd, or the shepherd of Israel, though both are true. He says mine. Whatever the day cost you, this sentence is still yours to say, out loud, in the present tense, before you sleep!
en.action_step: Say the verse out loud once, slowly, putting your own name in front of it. Then stop talking.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, tonight I am not asking for much. I just want to say it and mean it: You are my shepherd, and I shall not want. Quiet the part of me that keeps listing what is missing. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: We love because he first loved us.

traditional.text: We love him, because he first loved us.

modern.text: We love because he first loved us.

exegesis.context_note: John is writing to a church split by people who had left it, and much of the letter is about what real love looks like after a community has been hurt. The Greek puts 'he' first for emphasis: he loved us first. The whole sentence is seven words, and the argument turns entirely on the order of events.
key_themes: 爱是被给予的不是挣来的
exegesis.version_note: KJV 作 we love him,NIV 作 we love(无宾语);最早的抄本多无「him」,两个译法各有依据。
life_connection: 觉得自己爱得比对方多

en.meditation:
Most of us learned to love the way you learn a trade — by watching, and then by trying to earn back what we were given. Which is why so much loving is anxious. You track what you have put in. You notice what has not come back. In a marriage, in a long friendship, in the relationship you are least sure of, there is a running tally somewhere.

John cuts under all of it with one sentence and one word: first. You were loved before you performed, before you were chosen, before anyone owed you anything. Which means love is not a debt you are servicing. It is something you were handed, and can now spend freely.
en.action_step: Do one small kind thing tonight for someone close to you without letting them know, so that nothing can come back.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I keep a tally I do not admit to — in my marriage, in my friendships, in the relationship I am least sure of. Thank You that You loved me before there was anything to count. Loosen my grip on being owed. Let me love someone tomorrow without checking whether it comes back. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Then I acknowledged my sin to you and did not cover up my iniquity. I said, “I will confess my transgressions to the LORD.” And you forgave the guilt of my sin.

traditional.text: I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid. I said, I will confess my transgressions unto the Lord; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin. Selah.

modern.text: Then I acknowledged my sin to you and did not cover up my iniquity. I said, “I will confess my transgressions to the LORD.” And you forgave the guilt of my sin.

exegesis.context_note: Psalm 32 opens by calling the forgiven person happy, and the verse just before this describes what hiding did to David physically — bones wasting, strength drying up. 'Selah' is probably a musical direction, a pause. Whatever it meant technically, it lands here as a held breath after the word forgave.
key_themes: 赦免与认罪之间没有间隔
exegesis.version_note: KJV 与 NIV 都保留「我说:我要认罪」与「你就赦免了」的紧接语序,这个时序是本节的解经重心。
life_connection: 在心里反复措辞却不开口

en.meditation:
Read the timing in this verse, because it is the whole point. He says: I will confess. And then, in the same breath, before he has actually said anything out loud — you forgave. There is no gap. No interval where he is left standing in the doorway while a decision gets made about him.

As Christians we spend a great deal of energy bracing for that gap. We rehearse how it will go. We decide in advance how much to admit and how to word it so it sounds better. Tonight, when you finally say the honest sentence you have been avoiding, notice that nothing cold happens in between.
en.action_step: Say the sentence you have been rewording in your head. Say the plain version, not the softened one.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been drafting this confession instead of making it. Here is the plain version, without the softening. Thank You that there is no cold silence between my saying it and Your forgiving it. Take it, and let me stop carrying the rehearsal along with the thing itself. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with all of you.

traditional.text: Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means. The Lord be with you all.

modern.text: Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with all of you.

exegesis.context_note: This is Paul's closing blessing to a church anxious about the future and unsettled by rumours. 'Lord of peace' is a title he uses only here. The phrase translated 'by all means' is en panti tropō — in every manner or route — which widens the request rather than intensifying it.
key_themes: 平安由平安的主亲自给
「随时随事」包括你不会选的方式
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 by all means 与 NIV 的 in every way 同译 en panti tropō,意为「以各种途径」,是扩大范围而非加强语气。
life_connection: 把「求平安」讲成「求改变处境」

en.meditation:
Paul does not wish them peaceful circumstances. He asks the Lord of peace to give peace himself — the source handing over the thing, personally. Always, and by all means: which includes the ways you would not choose and cannot arrange.

So, tonight: are you waiting for peace to arrive as a change in your situation, when it may be trying to reach you by some other route entirely?
en.action_step: Ask for peace tonight without naming the circumstance you want changed. Just ask for the peace.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been asking You to change my situation and calling that asking for peace. Tonight I am asking for the peace itself, by whatever route You choose. Be with me until morning. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: The LORD will keep you from all harm—he will watch over your life;

traditional.text: The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul.

modern.text: The LORD will keep you from all harm—he will watch over your life;

exegesis.context_note: Psalm 121 is one of the songs pilgrims sang walking up to Jerusalem, and the whole psalm turns on a single Hebrew verb, shamar — to keep, guard, watch over — which appears six times in eight verses. It was sung on a road, by people away from home and aware of it.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 preserve 与 NIV 的 keep / watch over 同译希伯来 shamar,该词在诗篇 121 篇八节里出现六次。

en.meditation:
Twice in one short line: preserve, preserve. Hebrew poetry repeats when it wants to press something in.

And the second half is the wider promise. Not only from all evil, but he shall preserve thy soul — the part of you that gets worn down even when nothing dramatic happens. Tonight, both are being watched. Go to sleep guarded!
en.action_step: Before you lie down, say it once: the One keeping me does not sleep. Then let the day be over.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that You are keeping watch tonight — over the house, and over the part of me that nobody sees wearing down. I am going to stop guarding everything now, and sleep. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: For if you forgive other people when they sin against you, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

traditional.text: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:

modern.text: For if you forgive other people when they sin against you, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

exegesis.context_note: Jesus says this immediately after teaching the Lord's Prayer, and it is the one line he goes back to explain. The Greek paraptōma means a slip or a false step rather than a crime — the ordinary kind of hurt families cause each other. He is not making forgiveness a fee. He is describing what a forgiven person becomes.
key_themes: 赦免是已经领受的东西的流动
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 trespasses 与 NIV 的 sin against you 同译 paraptōma,本义是「失足、走偏」,比「罪行」轻。
life_connection: 和母亲之间没说开的事
觉得对方根本没道歉过

en.meditation:
This verse gets read as a transaction — forgive, and then you qualify. But Jesus has just finished teaching people to call God Father. He is not setting a fee. He is describing what happens to someone who has genuinely taken in how much was let go for them.

And the hardest place to test it is never the stranger. It is the person who has never once said sorry, who does not think there is anything to say sorry for, and who will be at the table again next month. That is the one this is about. Not because what they did was small, but because you were never meant to carry it this long.
en.action_step: Name the person. You do not have to feel warm about them. Just say to God that you are willing to stop charging them for it.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, You know the name I am thinking of. I do not feel forgiving, and I am not going to pretend I do. But I am willing. Take the account out of my hands tonight, before I add anything else to it. Thank You that You did not wait until I was sorry enough. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: May he give you the desire of your heart and make all your plans succeed.

traditional.text: Grant thee according to thine own heart, and fulfil all thy counsel.

modern.text: May he give you the desire of your heart and make all your plans succeed.

exegesis.context_note: Psalm 20 is a blessing the congregation sang over the king before he went out to battle — the whole psalm is other people praying for one person. That framing matters: this is not a promise God makes about outcomes, but a prayer a community dares to pray for someone it loves.
key_themes: 这是别人为你祷告的话
exegesis.version_note: 诗篇 20 篇整篇是会众为出征的王祷告的祝福词;本节是第三人称祝愿语气,不是应许。
life_connection: 不敢承认自己想要什么

en.meditation:
This is not a promise about getting what you want. It is a prayer other people prayed over someone they loved, out loud, before a hard day.

As Christians we can go strange about wanting things — as though naming a desire were a lack of faith. But here is a whole congregation saying it for their king. Tonight, let someone pray it for you. Or pray it for someone else, by name.
en.action_step: Pray this verse tonight for one specific person, using their name and the thing they actually want.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, tonight I pray this for someone else. You know what she wants and how long she has wanted it. Give her the desire of her heart. And where I have been embarrassed to want anything, let me be honest with You. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves receive from God.

traditional.text: Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.

modern.text: who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves receive from God.

exegesis.context_note: Paul opens this letter — his most personal and most bruised — with this sentence. The Greek stacks the same root five times in one verse: parakaleō, to call someone to your side. It is not cheerfulness. It is the act of coming and standing next to a person who cannot stand alone.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 与 NIV 都以 comfort 重复对应 parakaleō 的名动同源,原文里这一句连用五次同一字根。
life_connection: 自己还没好起来就要照顾别人
不知道怎么陪伴受苦的人

en.meditation:
Notice the direction of travel. Comfort comes in, and then it goes out — not as a duty added on top, but as the same thing continuing to move. Which also means nothing you have been through is stranded. It has somewhere to go.

So who, tonight, could be comforted by the exact thing you have needed comfort for?
en.action_step: Think of one person going through what you have been through. Send her a short message tomorrow — no advice, just presence.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have needed a lot of comfort lately and have not had much left over. Fill that up first. Then show me one person I could stand beside, using exactly what I have been through. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: But when you ask, you must believe and not doubt, because the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.

traditional.text: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.

modern.text: But when you ask, you must believe and not doubt, because the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.

exegesis.context_note: James is writing about asking God for wisdom. The Greek diakrinomenos is not the honest doubt of someone struggling; it means being divided in two — asking while simultaneously arranging not to need the answer. James is describing a hedge, not a weakness.
key_themes: 摇摆指的是两个心意不是脆弱
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 nothing wavering 与 NIV 的 not doubt 同译 diakrinomenos,原义近于「在自己里面两下分裂」,不是指偶尔的疑惑。
life_connection: 觉得自己信心不足所以不敢求
怕祷告没被应允是自己的错
一边求一边已经准备好失望

en.meditation:
This verse gets used against people who are already struggling to believe, which is almost the opposite of what James means. His word is not about wobbly faith. It is about being divided — asking God while quietly arranging a backup so you never have to depend on the answer.

So hear this tonight: you are not disqualified by finding faith hard. Ask anyway, and ask undivided. God is not looking for certainty. He is looking for someone who has actually turned toward Him!
en.action_step: Ask God for one thing tonight without immediately planning what you will do if He does not come through.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I ask You for things and then quietly arrange not to need You. Tonight I am asking without the backup plan. I do not have perfect faith and I am not going to pretend to. But I am turned toward You, and I am asking. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? Everything comes from you, and we have given you only what comes from your hand.

traditional.text: But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly after this sort? for all things come of thee, and of thine own have we given thee.

modern.text: But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? Everything comes from you, and we have given you only what comes from your hand.

exegesis.context_note: David prays this at the end of his life, after the people have given lavishly toward a temple he will not live to see built. It is not false modesty — he had genuinely organised the whole thing. He is saying that the capacity to give was itself given.
key_themes: 给出去的本来就是领受的
exegesis.version_note: KJV 与 NIV 都保留「who am I」的自问语气;和合本作「我算甚么」,三者语气一致。
life_connection: 拿自己的贡献和别人比
把成果完全归给自己的努力

en.meditation:
David had just organised the largest offering in Israel's history, and this is what he says about it: all things come of thee, and of thine own have we given thee.

He is not putting himself down. He is noticing that even the ability to give was handed to him. That is a restful thought at the end of a day spent producing things. What you gave today was real. It was also, first, given to you.
en.action_step: Name one thing you produced today, and then name where the capacity for it came from.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I gave what I had today, and I am tired. Thank You that even the ability to give was Yours first. Take the part of me that wants credit, and let me sleep without tallying what I contributed. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.

traditional.text: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,

modern.text: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.

exegesis.context_note: Paul wrote this to a church tearing itself apart over status and gifting, not to a wedding. The first quality he names, makrothumeō, is literally 'long-tempered' — the opposite of a short fuse. Every item on his list is a verb in Greek: love is not a feeling here but a set of things a person does.
key_themes: 这是婚礼经文也是日常经文
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 charity 与 NIV 的 love 同译 agapē;KJV 用 charity 是为区别于情感之爱,今日英语已不再传达此意。
life_connection: 被读了太多遍以致麻木的婚礼经文

en.meditation:
You have heard this at weddings until it stopped meaning anything. Try it somewhere else. Read it about last Tuesday. The first word on the list is patience, and in Greek it is literally long-tempered — the opposite of a short fuse. Not a feeling. A length. And the second is kindness, which is also something you do rather than something you feel.

Which is oddly good news for a tired woman in a long relationship. On the nights when the feeling is thin, love is still available to you. It is a thing you can do at eleven o'clock when you would rather not.
en.action_step: Pick one line from this verse and do it once tomorrow for the person you are closest to — deliberately, whether or not you feel it.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have heard these words so often that I stopped hearing them. Make them ordinary again — about the kitchen, about tomorrow morning, about the person I am hardest on. Where the feeling is thin, let me still choose the patience, and let me still choose the kindness. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Therefore encourage one another and build each other up, just as in fact you are doing.

traditional.text: Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also ye do.

modern.text: Therefore encourage one another and build each other up, just as in fact you are doing.

exegesis.context_note: Paul adds four words that are easy to skip: as in fact you are doing. He is not correcting them; he is naming something they already do and asking for more of it. The Greek oikodomeo, 'build up', is a construction word — adding a course of bricks, not offering a compliment.
key_themes: 建立是可以练习的动作
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 comfort 与 NIV 的 encourage 同译 parakaleō;和合本作「彼此劝慰」,兼含安慰与鼓励两面。
life_connection: 很久没有对人说过肯定的话
总在心里夸别人却不说出口

en.meditation:
Paul adds four words most of us read past: even as also ye do. He is not scolding them into it. He is naming something they are already doing and asking for more.

Building up is a construction word in Greek — laying another course of bricks, not paying a compliment. So: who did you build on today, and who did you mean to and didn't?
en.action_step: Send one person the specific sentence you thought about them today but did not say.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I notice good things about people and keep them to myself. That helps no one. Tomorrow, let me say one of them out loud. And where I am running low myself, send someone to say one to me. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die;

traditional.text: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:

modern.text: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die;

exegesis.context_note: Martha has just said she knows her brother will rise at the last day — correct doctrine, held at a safe distance. Jesus moves the whole thing into the present tense and into a person: I am. He says it standing four days late, outside a tomb, to a woman who has been grieving without him.
key_themes: 应许是一位而不是一个日期
exegesis.version_note: KJV 与 NIV 都保留「我就是」的现在式;耶稣把马大对「末日」的盼望拉回到眼前的一位。
life_connection: 安慰的话听起来都太远

en.meditation:
Martha said the right thing. He will rise again at the last day. It is true, and it is very far away, and it was not helping her at all that afternoon. Jesus does not correct her theology. He relocates it. Not a date — a person, standing in front of her, in the present tense: I am the resurrection.

Whatever you are grieving tonight, notice that the promise is not scheduled for later. It has a name, and it is here in the room with you, and it arrived four days late without apologising and without being one bit less true!
en.action_step: Say the name of the person you are missing. Then say the first three words of the verse out loud.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, some comfort is true and still too far away to reach me tonight. Thank You that Jesus did not offer Martha a date. He offered her Himself. Be that close to me. I am not asking to stop missing anyone. I am asking not to be alone with it. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Great peace have those who love your law, and nothing can make them stumble.

traditional.text: Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.

modern.text: Great peace have those who love your law, and nothing can make them stumble.

exegesis.context_note: The King James 'offend' meant to trip up, not to insult — the Hebrew is a stumbling-block image. Psalm 119 is an acrostic, the longest chapter in the Bible, entirely about loving God's instruction. This verse claims a specific benefit: not an easy life, but a stable footing.
key_themes: 大平安是稳固不是无事
爱神的话带来内在的定
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 nothing shall offend them 与 NIV 的 nothing can make them stumble 同译一个「绊脚」的意象,英文 offend 在 1611 年即指绊倒。
life_connection: 一句话就能毁掉一整天

en.meditation:
The old word 'offend' meant to trip, not to insult. So the promise is not that nothing will bother you. It is that nothing will take your feet out from under you.

That is a very specific kind of peace, and it is the one most of us actually need. Not a day without irritation — a day where the sharp remark at four o'clock does not end up owning the whole evening. Tonight, notice what tripped you, and notice that it does not get to keep you down.
en.action_step: Name the one thing that tripped you today. Say out loud that it does not get the rest of the night.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, one small thing today took my feet out from under me, and I have carried it for hours. I am putting it down now. Give me the kind of peace that stays steady underneath me, not the kind that depends on nothing going wrong all day. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree with one another in what you say and that there be no divisions among you,

traditional.text: Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.

modern.text: I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree with one another in what you say and that there be no divisions among you,

exegesis.context_note: Paul is writing to a church that had split into factions around favourite teachers. The Greek katartizō, translated 'perfectly joined together', is the word for setting a broken bone and for mending fishing nets — repair language, not uniformity language. He assumes the break has already happened.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 perfectly joined together 与 NIV 的 perfectly united 同译 katartizō,该词也用于「接骨」与「补网」。
life_connection: 家里或团队里的隐形站队
和某人已经很久只说客气话

en.meditation:
Paul's word for being joined together is the one used for setting a broken bone and for mending a torn net. Repair language. He is not asking a church to agree about everything; he is asking people who have already fractured to let the break be set. Setting a bone hurts, and it is done by someone else, and it takes longer than anyone wants.

Think about where you are quietly on one side of something tonight — in your family, at work, in a friendship that has cooled into politeness. Nothing dramatic has happened. That is usually how divisions actually start.
en.action_step: Name the relationship that has cooled into politeness. Decide one specific thing you will do this week to warm it.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, there is a relationship in my life that has gone quiet and polite, and I have let it. I do not want to be on a side. Show me the first move, even a small one, and give me the humility to make it before I am owed an apology. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Who is a God like you, who pardons sin and forgives the transgression of the remnant of his inheritance? You do not stay angry forever but delight to show mercy.

traditional.text: Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy.

modern.text: Who is a God like you, who pardons sin and forgives the transgression of the remnant of his inheritance? You do not stay angry forever but delight to show mercy.

exegesis.context_note: Micah's name means 'who is like the Lord', and here he turns his own name into the question. The book has spent six chapters on judgement before arriving at this. 'Delighteth' translates chaphets — to take pleasure in, to want to. Mercy is not described as a concession God makes but as something He enjoys.
key_themes: 赦免是祂的性情不是让步
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 delighteth in mercy 与 NIV 的 delight to show mercy 同译一个「以…为乐」的动词;和合本作「喜爱施恩」。

en.meditation:
Micah's name means 'who is like the Lord', and here he asks his own name as a question, at the end of six chapters of hard words about judgement. The answer he gives is not that God is lenient. It is that God delights in mercy — takes pleasure in it, wants to. Which is a very different picture from the one most of us carry around without ever examining it: a God who forgives correctly, but reluctantly, and who files the incident away for later.

So, honestly, tonight: which of those two are you actually expecting to meet when you pray?
en.action_step: Bring up the thing you have confessed several times already. Say it once more, and this time notice that He is not sighing.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been coming to You braced, as though Your forgiveness were something reluctantly given and nearly used up. Thank You that You delight in mercy. Not tolerate it. Delight in it. Let that go somewhere deeper in me tonight than my habit of apologising. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: A generous person will prosper; whoever refreshes others will be refreshed.

traditional.text: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

modern.text: A generous person will prosper; whoever refreshes others will be refreshed.

exegesis.context_note: The Hebrew image is agricultural: the one who waters gets watered. Proverbs is not promising a transaction — it is describing how a household, a village, an economy of kindness actually behaves over time. 'Made fat' was a picture of health and sufficiency, not excess.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 liberal soul shall be made fat 是希伯来式的丰足意象;NIV 作 generous person will prosper,取其义而舍其形象。

en.meditation:
For years I was the one who watered everyone, and I read this verse as a bill God had not paid.

What I did not expect was the form the return came in. Not from the people I poured into. From somewhere else entirely, and usually at a moment I had stopped asking. I still think the giving cost me something real. I also think I was watered.
en.action_step: Notice one place today where you were refreshed by someone you never poured into. Say thank you for it out loud.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been the one giving out for a long time, and I am dry. I am not going to pretend otherwise. Water me from wherever You choose, and let me notice it when it comes. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: For I am the LORD your God who takes hold of your right hand and says to you, Do not fear; I will help you.

traditional.text: For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.

modern.text: For I am the LORD your God who takes hold of your right hand and says to you, Do not fear; I will help you.

exegesis.context_note: In Hebrew the sequence matters: God takes the hand first, and only then speaks. The right hand is the working hand, the one that holds tools and weapons — so taking it is both comfort and interruption. The verb means to seize and keep hold of, not to steady lightly.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 hold thy right hand 与 NIV 的 takes hold of your right hand 同译一个「抓住并握牢」的动词,不是虚扶。

en.meditation:
Look at the order. He takes the hand first. The words come after.

That is not how reassurance usually works. We are told not to be afraid and then left to arrange it. Here the grip comes first, and 'fear not' is what gets said once you are already being held. Tonight, the hand is the point. The sentence is just what the hand is saying.
en.action_step: Put your own right hand out for a moment, and let the verse be about that hand. Then sleep.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I do not need an argument tonight. I need to be held. Thank You that You take hold first and speak afterwards. Keep hold of me until morning. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Jesus said, “Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.”

traditional.text: But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.

modern.text: Jesus said, “Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.”

exegesis.context_note: The disciples were turning families away — the mothers had brought children to be blessed and were being managed out of the way. Jesus rebukes the gatekeepers, not the parents. 'Suffer' is 1611 English for allow. The kingdom belongs to people with nothing to offer and no standing to protect.
key_themes: 耶稣责备的是拦阻的大人
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 suffer 是 1611 年英语的「容许」,非「受苦」;NIV 作 let,和合本作「让」,三者同义。

en.meditation:
The people being told off in this story are not the children. They are the adults who decided the children were an interruption to the real work. And notice who had brought them. Mothers, at the end of a day, carrying small people to someone they hoped would bless them — and being managed out of the way for it.

If today with your children was mostly noise and impatience and you are lying here feeling like the wrong sort of mother: He was never the one turning you away, and He is not starting tonight. That was always somebody else's idea of what mattered.
en.action_step: Say the name of each child in your care, and hand them over for the night. Then stop reviewing how today went.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, today with them was not my best. I was short, and I know it, and I have been going over it since they fell asleep. Thank You that You never treated children as an interruption, and that You are not treating me as one either. Take them for the night. Let me sleep instead of grading myself. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.

traditional.text: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.

modern.text: Whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.

exegesis.context_note: The Hebrew sether means a hiding place — somewhere concealed, not merely covered. The verb translated 'dwelleth' is about residing rather than visiting. The psalm distinguishes between passing through God's presence for help and actually living there.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 secret place 与 NIV 的 shelter 同译 sether「隐蔽处」;和合本作「隐密处」,强调不为人所见。
life_connection: 生活里没有一处不被看见

en.meditation:
Dwelleth, not visits. The psalm draws a line between coming to God for help and living in the shelter. And the word for secret place means hidden — somewhere out of view, where nobody is assessing you. Most of us do not have a single room like that any more.

So where, tonight, do you go to be unseen? And is it doing for you what this verse is offering?
en.action_step: Take five minutes tonight somewhere nobody can see you, and do nothing productive in them.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I am seen and assessed all day, and I am tired of being visible. Thank You that there is a place with You where nothing is being measured. Let me stay there tonight rather than just passing through. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: if my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, and I will forgive their sin and will heal their land.

traditional.text: If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

modern.text: if my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, and I will forgive their sin and will heal their land.

exegesis.context_note: God speaks this to Solomon the night after the temple is dedicated, as covenant terms for one nation. Read carefully, all four required actions are movements toward God rather than achievements: humbling, praying, seeking, turning. The Hebrew for 'seek my face' is about wanting the person, not the outcome.
key_themes: 四个动作都是转向不是表现
exegesis.version_note: 本节原是所罗门献殿时神对以色列的立约之言,今日应用需注意其国族圣约语境,不宜直接挪用为任何现代国家的应许。
life_connection: 想回头但不知道从哪开始
为家庭或群体的破碎难过

en.meditation:
Four things are asked here, and not one of them is an accomplishment. Humble yourself. Pray. Seek my face. Turn. Every one is a direction, not a performance. Which is a relief, because most of us assume that getting back to God requires first becoming someone worth coming back with. It does not. It requires turning around, which can be done from exactly where you are, tonight, in whatever state you are in.

And notice what He promises first in return, before the forgiving and before the healing of anything: I will hear. That is where it starts. He hears!
en.action_step: Turn once, in the smallest way available to you tonight: say one honest sentence to God instead of nothing.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been assuming I need to arrive in better shape before I come back. Tonight I am just turning around. I am not bringing anything except the turning. Thank You that You promised to hear before You promised anything else, and that hearing was never something I had to earn. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and when you pass through the rivers, they will not sweep over you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned; the flames will not set you ablaze.

traditional.text: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.

modern.text: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and when you pass through the rivers, they will not sweep over you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned; the flames will not set you ablaze.

exegesis.context_note: Isaiah writes to people who had already been through the water and the fire, not to people who were spared. The Hebrew says when, not if. Both images had literal history for the readers — the Red Sea behind them, the furnace of exile around them. The promise limits the damage; it does not cancel the crossing.
key_themes: 是「当你经过」不是「你不必经过」
exegesis.version_note: KJV 与 NIV 都作「当你经过」而非「若你经过」;这个「当」字是本节的解经重心,不可改成条件句。
life_connection: 正在一段过不去的日子里

en.meditation:
Read the small word carefully. When you pass through the waters. Not if. Not instead of. This was written to people who had already been through both. God does not promise them a life without deep water. He promises that the water will not close over their heads, and that He will be in it with them — which is a smaller promise than we want and a far more useful one than we expect.

If tonight you are in the middle of something nobody can shorten for you: you have not been abandoned to it. You have been accompanied into it.
en.action_step: Say where you are — in the water, in the fire, on the bank. Just name it accurately to God, without asking Him to fix it yet.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I am in the middle of it and nobody can shorten it for me. I have stopped asking You to. Tonight I am only asking You to be in here with me, and to keep the water from closing over my head. Thank You that You said when and not if. You knew. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled and do not be afraid.

traditional.text: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

modern.text: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled and do not be afraid.

exegesis.context_note: Jesus says this on the last night before the cross, with the worst still ahead of him. The peace behind the word is the Hebrew shalom: everything in its right place, not merely the absence of conflict. He gives it away on the night he has least of it himself.
key_themes: 恐惧被正视而非被否认
exegesis.version_note: KJV 与 NIV 都保留「不像世人所赐的」的对比句,是本节解经重心,不可略。

en.meditation:
He said this the night before the cross, which tells you what kind of peace He means. Not the absence of trouble; He had a great deal of trouble ahead.

As Christians we can wait for circumstances to cooperate and call that peace. His does not depend on the result, the reply, or the month ending well. It is His own settledness, handed over — and it can sit inside a night that is going badly.
en.action_step: Name one thing you are afraid of tonight, then say: this is real, and Jesus is still here. Let both stand.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, You know what I am carrying into tonight. Thank You that the peace Jesus gives does not wait for my situation to improve. Quiet my thoughts where they are racing, and remind me I am not alone in this room. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: And so we know and rely on the love God has for us. God is love. Whoever lives in love lives in God, and God in them.

traditional.text: And we have known and believed the love that God hath to us. God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him.

modern.text: And so we know and rely on the love God has for us. God is love. Whoever lives in love lives in God, and God in them.

exegesis.context_note: John pairs two verbs: we have known and we have believed. The second, pisteuō, carries the sense of leaning your weight on something. He is describing the distance between accepting a fact about God's love and actually resting on it — a gap most believers live in for years.
key_themes: 爱是神的本质不是情绪
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 believed 与 NIV 的 rely on 同译 pisteuō;此处的「信」含「靠上去」之意,不只是认知同意。
life_connection: 觉得神爱别人比爱自己多

en.meditation:
John uses two verbs, and the gap between them is where most of us live. We have known — and we have believed. The second one means leaning your weight on something. You can know God loves you and still not put any weight on it. You can teach it, sing it, and go to bed at night quietly running on the assumption that you are tolerated.

So which is it, tonight — known, or leaned on?
en.action_step: Say it in the leaning form: not God is love, but God loves me, and I am going to sleep on that.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I know this and I do not lean on it. Tonight I want to put some weight on it. You love me. Not the version of me I would prefer to show You — me, as I actually was today. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: In peace I will lie down and sleep, for you alone, LORD, make me dwell in safety.

traditional.text: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, Lord, only makest me dwell in safety.

modern.text: In peace I will lie down and sleep, for you alone, LORD, make me dwell in safety.

exegesis.context_note: David wrote this while under threat, and the Hebrew keeps two separate acts — lying down, and sleeping — because for an anxious person they are not the same thing. 'Only' is emphatic: not the walls, not the guards. Sleep here is an act of trust, which is why it is so hard to do.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 both lay me down…and sleep 保留了希伯来原文的两个动作;和合本作「我必安然躺下睡觉」,NIV 同。
life_connection: 夜里反复检查门窗和手机

en.meditation:
The Hebrew keeps them as two separate acts: I will lie down, and I will sleep. Anyone who has spent a night staring at the ceiling knows they are not the same thing.

And the word that carries the verse is only. Not the locked door, not the plan for tomorrow, not your own vigilance. Sleep is where you stop guarding and let Someone else do it. Go and do that now!
en.action_step: Put the phone down first, before anything else. Then say the verse once and stop talking.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I am lying down but I have not stopped guarding. Take the watch from me tonight. You alone make me dwell in safety — not the checking, not the planning. I am going to sleep now. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: You will keep in perfect peace those whose minds are steadfast, because they trust in you.

traditional.text: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.

modern.text: You will keep in perfect peace those whose minds are steadfast, because they trust in you.

exegesis.context_note: The Hebrew literally says shalom shalom — peace peace — repeating the word for emphasis, the way English might say 'utterly at peace'. The word for 'stayed' means propped, leaned, supported: a mind resting its weight on something outside itself rather than holding itself up.
key_themes: 平安与心思的方向相连
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 perfect peace 译自希伯来 shalom shalom(重复以示极致);和合本作「十分平安」,NIV 作 perfect peace。
life_connection: 把停不下来当成责任感

en.meditation:
The Hebrew says it twice — peace, peace — because one was not enough for what it is describing.

And the condition is not that your mind stops. It is where your mind is leaning. The word means propped up, resting its weight on something. A mind at three in the morning is not still; it is holding itself up. Let it lean somewhere tonight.
en.action_step: When your mind starts running tonight, do not argue with it. Say one true sentence about God and let your thoughts lean there.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, my mind will not stop tonight and arguing with it has never worked. I am not asking You to switch it off. I am asking to lean it somewhere. Hold my thinking steady until I sleep. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.

traditional.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

modern.text: Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.

exegesis.context_note: Jesus says this to crowds worn down by religious rules that had grown heavy and very detailed. 'Rest' is anapauō — the breath a labourer takes when the load comes off, not sleep. He does not ask them to qualify first; the invitation is aimed at whoever arrives already tired.
key_themes: 耶稣主动就近疲惫的人
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 labour and are heavy laden 强调劳动,NIV 的 weary and burdened 强调被压;两者合起来才是原文的完整画面。
life_connection: 带完孩子后半夜仍睡不着
工作日结束却停不下来
觉得必须先把自己收拾好才配来

en.meditation:
He does not say come when you have sorted yourself out. He says come — as you are, at the end of a day that took more than it gave.

As Christians we can turn even this into an instruction we are failing at: rest properly, be at peace, stop striving. But look again at the verb you are given. It is not rest. It is come. The resting is His half of the sentence, and He has never once needed help with His half of anything.
en.action_step: Say the heaviest thing on your mind out loud, then: I am giving this to You tonight. Leave it there until morning.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I am tired in a way sleep alone will not fix. Thank You that Your invitation is still open this late, and that it does not require me to arrive rested before I come. Take the weight out of my hands and hold it there until morning. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: For from him and through him and for him are all things. To him be the glory forever! Amen.

traditional.text: For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen.

modern.text: For from him and through him and for him are all things. To him be the glory forever! Amen.

exegesis.context_note: Paul has spent three chapters on the hardest question he knows — what God is doing with Israel — and does not arrive at an answer. He arrives at this instead. The doxology is what he says when the argument runs out, not what he says when it resolves.
key_themes: 三个介词划出全部范围
颂赞出现在讲不下去的地方
exegesis.version_note: KJV 与 NIV 都保留 of / through / to 三个介词的并列;这三个介词分别指来源、途径与归属,缺一不可。
life_connection: 想不通神为什么允许某些事

en.meditation:
Paul has just spent three chapters on the hardest question in his letter and does not solve it. This is what he says instead — not the conclusion of the argument, but what he does when the argument runs out. Which is worth noticing, because most of us treat unanswered questions as a failure of faith. Paul treats one as a reason to worship. He does not know. He says so. And then he says: of him, and through him, and to him.

So what would it change tonight to stop demanding the answer and let the thing be bigger than you instead?
en.action_step: Name the question you cannot resolve. Then say the verse over it, without pretending the question is settled.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, there is something I cannot make sense of, and I have been treating that as a problem with my faith. Tonight I am going to let it be bigger than me instead of solved. Of You, and through You, and to You are all things — including the part I do not understand. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: As water reflects the face, so one's life reflects the heart.

traditional.text: As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.

modern.text: As water reflects the face, so one's life reflects the heart.

exegesis.context_note: The Hebrew is compressed and has been read two ways: a heart reveals the person, or one heart answers another as a face answers its reflection. Ancient readers had no mirrors — only still water, which had to be undisturbed to show anything. Both readings need stillness.
key_themes: 长久的关系里才照得出来
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 so the heart of man to man 与 NIV 的 one's life reflects the heart 是两种解读路径;希伯来原文简略,两解皆有依据。
life_connection: 在关系里觉得没被真正认识
长年相处却越来越客气

en.meditation:
They had no mirrors. To see your own face you found still water and waited for it to settle. Any disturbance and the picture broke. Which is most of what is wrong with our closest relationships. Not that we are not known — that nothing is ever still long enough to reflect anything. You come in at seven, the day is still churning, and you talk about logistics until you sleep.

Someone close to you is trying to see you, and the water has not settled once this week. It does not take an evening. Let it settle tonight — even for ten minutes, even badly!
en.action_step: Sit with the person closest to you tonight for ten minutes with nothing running — no screen, no logistics. Let it be quiet.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I am close to people who do not really see me, and some of that is my own doing — I never stop moving long enough to be seen. Give me the courage to be still with someone tonight. Let something true get reflected back, even briefly. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: How good and pleasant it is when God's people live together in unity!

traditional.text: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!

modern.text: How good and pleasant it is when God's people live together in unity!

exegesis.context_note: This was sung by pilgrims travelling to the festivals — families walking together for days, which is when unity stops being a sentiment. The verb means literally to sit or dwell together. The psalm goes on to compare it to oil running down and dew falling: things that come from above and spread downward.
key_themes: 同住是具体的不是抽象的
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 dwell together 与 NIV 的 live together 同译一个「同住」的动词,指实际住在一起,不是抽象的团契。

en.meditation:
This was sung by families walking to Jerusalem together for days at a time, which is exactly when unity stops being an idea and becomes a discipline. And the word is dwell — actually living in the same rooms as people, not feeling warm about them from a distance. Note also that the psalm goes on to describe unity as oil poured out and dew falling: things that arrive from above rather than being generated by everyone trying harder.

If your house is tense tonight, that is not proof of failure. It is a house with real people in it.
en.action_step: Do one small thing tonight that lowers the temperature in your home rather than proving a point.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, my house is not always a peaceful place, and I am part of why. Thank You that unity is something You pour down from above rather than something we manufacture by all trying harder at once. Let some of it reach this house tonight, and let it start with me. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: The LORD replied, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”

traditional.text: And he said, My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest.

modern.text: The LORD replied, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”

exegesis.context_note: After the golden calf, God offers to send a messenger ahead rather than go himself. Moses refuses that deal. The Hebrew here is literally 'my face' — presence in person, not a representative. Moses asks for God rather than for an outcome, and the rest comes attached to the presence.
exegesis.version_note: 路德 1912 德文版此节作「引导」而非「使你得安息」,做德语版时须留意;KJV / NIV / 和合本均作「安息」。
life_connection: 独自撑着一个家的夜晚

en.meditation:
Moses is offered a good outcome without God's own presence, and turns it down. That is the whole negotiation.

As Christians we usually ask the other way round: fix this, and You need not come yourself. But notice what the rest is attached to here. Not the solved problem. The presence. Which is worth knowing tonight, if nothing is solved and you still have to sleep.
en.action_step: Tonight, instead of asking God to fix something, ask Him simply to stay. Say it in your own words.
