prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, most of my praying is a list of things I want changed. Tonight I would rather have You near than have it all settled. Stay with me in the unresolved part, and give me the rest that comes with You. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Whoever conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy.

traditional.text: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.

modern.text: Whoever conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy.

exegesis.context_note: Proverbs uses the same verb here as in 17:9, but pointed the other way: covering someone else's offence is love, covering your own is corrosion. Note that the promise is mercy, not consequences removed — and that confessing and forsaking are held together as one movement.
key_themes: 遮掩自己的罪与遮盖别人的罪相反
exegesis.version_note: 本节的「遮掩」与箴言 17:9「遮掩人的过犯」用同一动词但方向相反:遮盖别人是爱,遮掩自己是害。
life_connection: 有件事一直没对任何人说

en.meditation:
Same verb as covering someone else's offence, aimed the other direction. Covering theirs is love. Covering your own quietly rots. And notice that the verse holds two halves together: confesseth, and forsaketh. Saying it without leaving it is not what is being described here, and neither is quietly leaving it while never once admitting it happened. Both, or neither.

So what have you been carrying entirely on your own, not because it is unspeakable, but because saying it out loud would cost you something you are not ready to pay?
en.action_step: Say the thing to God tonight. If it needs saying to a person, decide who, and when this week.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been holding something on my own because telling anyone would cost me. It is costing me more to keep it. Here it is. Give me the courage for whatever comes next, and for whoever else needs to hear it. Thank You that what I find waiting here is mercy and not a reckoning. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.

traditional.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.

modern.text: Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.

exegesis.context_note: The old English 'be careful' meant full of care, anxious — not cautious. Paul does not tell them to stop feeling; he gives them somewhere to put it. The Greek for 'requests' is specific and itemised, the language of a written petition rather than a general feeling.
key_themes: 焦虑要换成具体的祈求
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 be careful for nothing 是 1611 年英语的「不要挂虑」,非「不要小心」;NIV 作 do not be anxious。

en.meditation:
Paul is not telling you to stop feeling anxious. He is telling you where to put it, which is a very different instruction.

And the word for requests means specific, itemised things — the language of a petition, not a mood. So do not pray about your worry tonight. Pray about the actual item. Name it, hand it over, and thank Him on the way!
en.action_step: Write down the worry as one specific request. Not the feeling — the item. Then pray that sentence.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been praying about my anxiety in general and it has not helped. Here is the specific thing. I am handing You this one item tonight, and thanking You in advance for how You will handle it. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Let love and faithfulness never leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.

traditional.text: Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them about thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart:

modern.text: Let love and faithfulness never leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.

exegesis.context_note: Chesed and emet — steady kindness and truthfulness — appear together throughout the Old Testament as a pair describing God's own character. Two images follow: binding around the neck, which is visible and worn daily, and writing on the heart, which is internal and permanent.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 mercy and truth 与 NIV 的 love and faithfulness 同译 chesed 与 emet;这两个词在旧约中常成对出现,形容神自己。

en.meditation:
Two words that the Old Testament almost never separates: steady kindness, and telling the truth. Together they describe God's own character.

Which is why holding only one of them always goes wrong. Kindness without truth quietly becomes management — steering people rather than levelling with them. Truth without kindness becomes an assault carried out with a clear conscience. Most of us lean hard one way, and it feels like a personality rather than a choice. The person on the other end of that lean usually knows exactly which way we go.
en.action_step: Decide which of the two you lean away from. Practise that one tomorrow, with one specific person.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I lean one way and it costs the people around me. Bind both of them to me — the kindness and the honesty together, not one purchased at the expense of the other. Write them somewhere deep enough that they still hold when I am tired. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: This is the confidence we have in approaching God: that if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.

traditional.text: And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us:

modern.text: This is the confidence we have in approaching God: that if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.

exegesis.context_note: John promises hearing, not compliance — and the early church always read Mark 11:24 alongside this. 'According to his will' is not a loophole; it is the condition that keeps prayer from being a mechanism. The Greek for confidence is parrhesia again: freedom of speech before someone in authority.
key_themes: 应许的是垂听不是照办
exegesis.version_note: KJV 与 NIV 都止于 he heareth us「祂听我们」,并未应许照所求成就;这个界限是本节的解经重心。

en.meditation:
Read exactly what is promised. He hears us. Not: He does it.

As Christians we can quietly resent that, until we consider what the alternative would be — a God who acts on every request we have ever made in a bad week. Being heard is not the consolation prize. It is the thing. Someone with more sense than you has your request and is not ignoring it.
en.action_step: Pray for the thing you have been asking about, and then say: I know You heard that. Leave it there.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been asking about this for a long time and hearing nothing back. Thank You that being heard is not the same as being ignored. I am leaving it with You again tonight, and I am going to stop checking. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them.

traditional.text: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.

modern.text: For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them.

exegesis.context_note: The context is reconciliation: Jesus has just described how to deal with an offence between two people, and 'two or three' originally referred to witnesses. The wider use of the verse for any gathering came later, and is fair enough — but it began as a promise about people doing the hard work of mending something.
exegesis.version_note: 本节的上下文是处理弟兄之间的过犯,「两三个人」原指见证人;广义应用于聚集是后来的传统,须知其来源。
life_connection: 觉得自己的小圈子不够属灵

en.meditation:
Two or three. Not a full room, not a good turnout — two.

And notice where Jesus says it: right after describing two people trying to sort out a wrong between them. So He is not only in the singing. He is in the awkward conversation, in your kitchen, with the one friend who still answers the phone. Whatever is left of your circle, you are not below the minimum. He counts it as enough!
en.action_step: Message one person tonight and ask to pray together this week. Two is enough.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, my two or three have got scattered, and I have let it happen. Thank You that You never set a minimum turnout. Bring one person back into range this week, and give me the humility to ask. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: And over all these virtues put on love, which binds them all together in perfect unity.

traditional.text: And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.

modern.text: And over all these virtues put on love, which binds them all together in perfect unity.

exegesis.context_note: Paul has just listed a set of qualities — compassion, kindness, humility, patience — as items of clothing. Love is the outer garment or the belt that holds the rest in place. Every verb in the passage is about putting on: these are things you do, not moods you wait for.
key_themes: 爱是穿在最外面的那件
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 bond of perfectness 与 NIV 的 binds them together in perfect unity 同译一个「带子、腰带」的意象;和合本作「联络全德的」。
life_connection: 以为爱是感觉不是选择

en.meditation:
There was a year in my marriage when nothing was wrong and nothing was warm. We were kind, we were patient, we divided the week fairly. Everything on Paul's list was technically present and the whole thing still felt like an arrangement. What I had left off was the last item — the one he calls the belt. Love, put on deliberately, on top of the rest, on evenings when I did not feel like it.

It did not fix anything quickly. It held things together while they slowly got better, which I have come to think is what a belt is for.
en.action_step: Choose one deliberate act of love tonight for the person you have been merely fair to.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been kind and fair and careful, and somewhere in that I stopped actually loving anyone on purpose. Show me the one thing to put on tonight. Not the feeling, which I do not have on order — the act. Hold together what has been sitting loose between us for longer than I have admitted. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: I have told you these things, so that in me you may have peace. In this world you will have trouble. But take heart! I have overcome the world.

traditional.text: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.

modern.text: I have told you these things, so that in me you may have peace. In this world you will have trouble. But take heart! I have overcome the world.

exegesis.context_note: Jesus says this in the last minutes before Gethsemane. The Greek tharseite is closer to 'take courage' than 'cheer up' — it is what a commander says, not what a friend says at a party. And 'I have overcome' is in the perfect tense: already done, before the cross had happened.
key_themes: 平安在祂里面不在环境
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 be of good cheer 与 NIV 的 take heart 同译 tharseō「壮胆」,不是「高兴起来」;这个区别很重要。
life_connection: 怀疑信主为什么还这么难

en.meditation:
Hear both halves and do not soften either one. In this world you will have trouble — He says it plainly, and He was right.

And then: I have overcome. Already finished, in the perfect tense, said before the cross had even happened. So the peace on offer tonight is not the absence of trouble. It is that the outcome was settled before your trouble started. Take courage!
en.action_step: Name tonight's trouble honestly. Then say the last five words of the verse over it.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, it has been one thing after another and I am tired of being told to be positive. Thank You that Jesus never promised otherwise. Give me courage rather than cheerfulness tonight, and let me rest in the part that is already finished. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, since as members of one body you were called to peace. And be thankful.

traditional.text: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.

modern.text: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, since as members of one body you were called to peace. And be thankful.

exegesis.context_note: The Greek brabeuō is what an umpire does at the games — it means to arbitrate, to make the call. So this is not a suggestion to feel peaceful. It is an instruction to let peace be the thing that decides when there is a dispute inside you. Paul adds three words: and be thankful.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 rule 与 NIV 的 rule 同译 brabeuō,原指运动会裁判的判定;和合本作「作主」,亦有「决断」之意。

en.meditation:
The word for rule is what an umpire does — makes the call, settles the dispute. So Paul is not telling you to feel peaceful. He is telling you to let peace be the deciding vote when there are two voices going at once in your chest. Not the loudest one. Not the most anxious one, which usually sounds the most responsible. The one that leaves you at peace when you sit with it.

And then, almost as an afterthought: be thankful. As Christians we usually try those in the wrong order.
en.action_step: Where you are torn tonight, notice which option leaves you at peace and let that be the vote.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, there are two voices in me tonight and the anxious one is louder. Let Your peace make the call instead. Settle the dispute in my chest tonight, and while it settles, give me one thing I can honestly be thankful for. In that order, for once. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: And when you stand praying, if you hold anything against anyone, forgive them, so that your Father in heaven may forgive you your sins.

traditional.text: And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.

modern.text: And when you stand praying, if you hold anything against anyone, forgive them, so that your Father in heaven may forgive you your sins.

exegesis.context_note: Jesus attaches this directly to a promise about prayer — the two are not separate subjects. 'If ye have ought against any' assumes you will; it is not a rebuke. Standing was the ordinary posture for prayer at the time, so this is about the everyday moment of praying, not a special occasion.
key_themes: 站着祷告是当时的姿势
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 ought against any 与 NIV 的 hold anything against anyone 同义;「ought」是 1611 年英语的「任何事」,非「应该」。
life_connection: 祷告时想起某个人就卡住
怕饶恕等于说对方没错

en.meditation:
Notice the word if. Jesus assumes there will be someone. He is not shocked that you are holding something. And notice where He puts it — right in the middle of praying, as part of the same motion. Not a separate spiritual project to schedule for later.

So whose face came to mind just now, before you finished reading the verse?
en.action_step: Say that person's name to God tonight, and say the one sentence you would rather not say about them.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, a face came to mind straight away and I would rather it had not. I am not going to pretend it is nothing. Help me let it go tonight, before it settles in any deeper. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: And now these three remain: faith, hope and love. But the greatest of these is love.

traditional.text: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.

modern.text: And now these three remain: faith, hope and love. But the greatest of these is love.

exegesis.context_note: Paul is contrasting these three with the spiritual gifts the Corinthians were competing over — those, he says, will stop. The verb menō means to remain or abide: to still be there when other things have ended. Love is greatest partly because it is the one that continues past this life.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 abideth 与 NIV 的 remain 同译 menō「存留、住下」;和合本作「常存」,指持续存在而非暂时。

en.meditation:
Paul has just told a church obsessed with impressive gifts that all of them will stop. Then: these three remain. The word means to still be there when the rest has ended. Which is a strange and steadying thing to read in a long relationship, on an ordinary Tuesday night, when nothing dramatic is happening and nothing feels particularly remarkable.

The impressive parts of a marriage or a friendship do stop. The remarkable early stretch stops. What remains is faith, hope, and this stubborn ordinary thing that keeps choosing. And Paul says that last one is the biggest thing in the room!
en.action_step: Look at the longest relationship in your life and name one way love has remained after other things stopped.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, some of what was exciting in my closest relationships has quietly ended, and I have grieved that more than I have said. Thank You that love is the part that remains. Let me see it where it is still there tonight, plain and unimpressive and holding. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Then you will call on me and come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.

traditional.text: Then shall ye call upon me, and ye shall go and pray unto me, and I will hearken unto you.

modern.text: Then you will call on me and come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.

exegesis.context_note: This sits between the famous promise about plans and the promise about seeking with all your heart — all three sentences were sent to people in exile. The Hebrew for 'hearken' means to bend the ear toward, an active posture rather than passive hearing.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 hearken 与 NIV 的 listen 同译一个「侧耳倾听」的希伯来词,比「听见」更主动。
life_connection: 在漫长的等待里失去信心

en.meditation:
Three verbs on your side: call, come, pray. One on His: I will hearken. And the Hebrew word is not simply hearing. It is bending toward — the posture of someone leaning in because they do not want to miss it.

That was written to people a thousand miles from home who had every reason to believe God had stopped listening. Tonight, so is this.
en.action_step: Pray one sentence tonight assuming He is leaning in, not assuming He is busy.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been praying as though You were half listening. Thank You that You bend toward it. Here is tonight's sentence, and I am going to say it believing You are leaning in. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it.

traditional.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

modern.text: Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it.

exegesis.context_note: Proverbs states general truths about how life usually works, not guarantees about individual cases — the same book says a wise son makes a glad father, and Scripture is full of exceptions. Some scholars read the Hebrew as 'according to his way', meaning according to the child's own bent. Either reading rules out using this verse to assign blame.
key_themes: 「当行的道」也可解作「照他的性情」
exegesis.version_note: 本节是箴言体的通则,不是个别的应许;把它读成对每个孩子的保证会给父母带来不该有的罪疚,这是解经上的重要界限。

en.meditation:
Proverbs tells you how things generally go. It is not a contract, and it was never meant to be read as one — which matters enormously if your child has walked away and you have been quietly serving a sentence for it. Some read the Hebrew as: according to his way, meaning according to the particular child in front of you rather than a single method for all of them.

Either way, this verse is a wise general truth about the long shaping of a life. It is not a verdict on you at eleven o'clock at night, and it never has been.
en.action_step: If you have been blaming yourself for how a child turned out, say one sentence tonight putting them back in God's hands.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have used this verse against myself for years. Tonight I am putting it down. I did not have the power to guarantee an outcome, and I never did. Take my child back into Your hands, where they have been the whole time. Let me sleep without the verdict. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.

traditional.text: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.

modern.text: When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.

exegesis.context_note: David wrote this, according to the heading, when he had been seized in Gath — genuinely cornered, genuinely afraid. The Hebrew makes no attempt to deny the fear. It simply places trust inside the same moment rather than after it.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 What time I am afraid 是 1611 年英语的「每当我害怕的时候」;NIV 作 when I am afraid,和合本作「我惧怕的时候」。

en.meditation:
Six words in English, and not one of them pretends the fear is gone. That is what makes it usable. He does not say: when I stop being afraid, I will trust. He says the two happen in the same moment, in the same body, at the same time.

So what would it look like tonight to be afraid and to trust, without waiting for the first to finish?
en.action_step: Say both halves out loud in one breath: I am afraid of this, and I trust You.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I am afraid tonight and I have stopped apologising for it. I am not waiting until the fear passes to trust You. Both at once, then. Hold me while I am still afraid. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.

traditional.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

modern.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.

exegesis.context_note: John wrote against teachers who denied sin was real at all. The Greek for 'confess' is homologeō — literally to say the same thing: to describe something the way God already describes it, without dressing it up or exaggerating it. 'Faithful and just' sit together on purpose; forgiveness is a promise kept, not a mood.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 与 NIV 都把 faithful and just 并列——赦免不是神心软的例外,而是祂守约的必然。
life_connection: 睡前反复回放自己说错的话

en.meditation:
Faithful and just. Not merciful and lenient — those would be different words. Which means forgiveness here is not God making an exception for you on a good day. It is God keeping His word, which He has never once failed to do about anything.

So you are not asking for a favour tonight, and you are not hoping to catch Him in a generous mood. You are asking Him to be what He already is. That is a very different thing to walk into a room holding!
en.action_step: Say one specific thing to God tonight that you would rather gloss over. One sentence. Then stop — do not add the self-criticism.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that I am not asking for a favour tonight but for something You have already promised. Here is the thing I would rather have kept quiet about. Cleanse it, and let me sleep tonight without replaying the whole thing twice more. Help me wake up gentler tomorrow with the people who live closest to me. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one's life for one's friends.

traditional.text: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

modern.text: Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one's life for one's friends.

exegesis.context_note: Jesus says this hours before the cross, and then, remarkably, calls the disciples friends rather than servants. The Greek verb for laying down means to set something aside — it can describe a single act or a repeated one. Most people who live this verse do it in instalments.
key_themes: 舍命通常不是一次而是许多次
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 lay down his life 与 NIV 的 lay down one's life 同译一个「放下、交出」的动词;不限于殉道,亦含日常的舍己。
life_connection: 为别人放弃自己的计划
怀疑这样的付出值不值得

en.meditation:
We read this as one heroic moment, because that is how Jesus fulfilled it. But the Greek verb simply means to set something down, and it can be done once or a thousand times. Which is how most love actually gets laid down: in instalments. The career you did not take. The years given to someone who needed them. The evening handed over again, quietly, to a person who will not remember this particular one.

If that has been your life and you have privately wondered whether it counted for much, read the first four words again. Greater love hath no man.
en.action_step: Name one thing you have laid down for someone. Do not justify it — just let it be named.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have given years to people in small pieces and sometimes wondered whether any of it registered. Thank You that You called this the greatest love there is, and that You did not require it to be dramatic. Let me lay down tomorrow's portion without resentment. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: He says, “Be still, and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth.”

traditional.text: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.

modern.text: He says, “Be still, and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth.”

exegesis.context_note: The psalm is about a city under threat, not a quiet retreat. The Hebrew verb means something closer to 'let go' or 'stop fighting' than 'be quiet' — it is what you say to someone still struggling. Stillness here is the surrender of control, not a mood of calm.
exegesis.version_note: 希伯来原文的「安静」近于「松手、住手」,不是「保持安静」;这个差别是本节最常被误读之处。

en.meditation:
The Hebrew is closer to let go than to be quiet. It is what you say to someone who is still struggling: stop. Drop your hands.

As Christians we hear this as an invitation to peaceful feelings, and then fail at it. It is not that. It is an instruction to stop managing the outcome. The knowing comes afterwards, and it comes to hands that have opened.
en.action_step: Physically open your hands for thirty seconds tonight while you say the verse. Let the gesture do the arguing.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I have been holding on to this with both hands all day. Let go, You said. So I am opening my hands tonight, and I am going to leave them open. You are God and I am not, and that is a relief. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.

traditional.text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

modern.text: Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.

exegesis.context_note: In Greek this continues the sentence before it — humble yourselves, and throw your anxiety onto him. The two are one movement, which means handing worry over is an act of humility rather than weakness. Epiriptō is the motion of heaving a pack onto a pack animal: one decisive transfer.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 casting 与 NIV 的 cast 同译 epiriptō,是把包袱整个甩上牲口背的动作;和合本作「卸给」。
life_connection: 熄灯后开始复盘一整天
为家人的处境反复担忧
觉得自己的焦虑不值得拿出来

en.meditation:
The verb is not 'share' or 'discuss'. It is the motion of swinging a load off your own back and onto an animal that can carry it. One movement, and then your hands are empty. And it is grammatically joined to the sentence before: humble yourselves, and cast. Which reframes the whole thing. Keeping hold of your worry is not strength. It is a quiet insistence that you are the one who has to carry it.

So what are you still carrying because handing it over would mean admitting you cannot?
en.action_step: Name the worry, then say: this is not mine to carry tonight. Put it down before you get into bed.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I hold on to my worries because letting go feels like admitting I cannot manage. Tonight I am admitting it. Here is the whole load, swung over onto You. Thank You that You care about the small things I would be embarrassed to say out loud. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Do everything in love.

traditional.text: Let all your things be done with charity.

modern.text: Do everything in love.

exegesis.context_note: This is the shortest of Paul's closing commands, tucked between practical instructions about travel and money. Five words in English, four in Greek. It does not add a task; it names the manner in which the existing ones are to be done.
key_themes: 不是做更多而是怎么做
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 with charity 与 NIV 的 in love 同译 en agapē;KJV 用 charity 是为与情感之爱区别,今日英语已不再传达此意。
life_connection: 做了一堆事却越来越冷淡

en.meditation:
Four words in Greek, dropped in between instructions about travel arrangements and collections.

And notice it does not add anything to your list. It does not say do more. It says do the same things differently. Which is either a relief or a challenge tonight, depending on how you did them today!
en.action_step: Look back at one thing you did today. Ask how it would have looked done in love, and carry that into tomorrow.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I got a lot done today and I am not sure how much of it was done in love. Thank You that You are not adding to my list. Change the way I do it tomorrow, starting at home. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Why, my soul, are you downcast? Why so disturbed within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise him, my Savior and my God.

traditional.text: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.

modern.text: Why, my soul, are you downcast? Why so disturbed within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise him, my Savior and my God.

exegesis.context_note: This line repeats three times across Psalms 42 and 43 — a refrain the writer keeps returning to because it has not been resolved. He asks himself the question twice and does not answer it. What he does instead is speak to himself rather than merely listen to himself, and point the conversation forward.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 cast down 与 NIV 的 downcast 同译一个「弯下、垂下」的希伯来词;本节在诗篇 42-43 篇中重复三次,是全诗的副歌。

en.meditation:
He asks the question twice and never answers it. That detail is worth a great deal, because most of us assume being downcast requires an explanation before it is allowed. What he does instead is talk to himself rather than only listen to himself. There is a difference. Listening to yourself at eleven at night is how a low evening becomes a low week. Speaking to yourself — hope thou in God — is a different act entirely.

And notice the tense of what he says: I shall yet praise him. Not I feel like it now. Yet. Later. He is not lying about tonight; he is refusing to let tonight have the final word.
en.action_step: Say one sentence out loud to yourself tonight instead of about yourself. Use the future tense.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I am low tonight and I cannot fully explain why, and I have been treating that as a failure. Thank You that the psalm asks the question twice and never answers it either. Let me speak to myself instead of listening to myself. I will praise You again. Not tonight, maybe. But I will. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.

traditional.text: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven:

modern.text: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.

exegesis.context_note: The two verbs are distinct in Greek: krinō is to assess or discriminate, katadikazō is to pass sentence. Jesus is not banning discernment — Luke's Gospel is full of it. He is banning the move from noticing to sentencing. The next verse adds that the measure you use comes back to you.
key_themes: 宽容的量器会回到自己身上
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 judge / condemn 分译两个不同的希腊词:前者是「分辨、评断」,后者是「定罪」;二者不可混为一谈。

en.meditation:
Two different words are used here, and the difference matters. The first means to assess. The second means to pass sentence. Jesus is not asking you to stop noticing things about people; He notices constantly. He is asking you to stop moving from noticing to sentencing — the small internal courtroom that convenes over someone's parenting, or their marriage, or how they look now.

And the reason given is not moral superiority. It is that the measure comes back. Whatever standard you are running on other people is the one running on you at three in the morning.
en.action_step: Notice one person you quietly sentenced today. Drop the sentence, and see whether anything loosens in you too.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I hold a private court most days and I am the judge in all of it. I am harder on myself than on anyone else in that courtroom, and I have started to suspect the two things are connected. Let me stop sentencing people tonight. Including me. Especially me. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.

traditional.text: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.

modern.text: Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.

exegesis.context_note: Paul has just listed what to put away — bitterness, anger, shouting — and this is what replaces them. The Greek eusplanchnos literally means having good inward parts: compassion felt physically, in the gut. The measure given is not fairness but the way God has already treated you.
key_themes: 比照的标准是神怎样待你
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 tenderhearted 与 NIV 的 compassionate 同译 eusplanchnos,字面是「内脏柔软」,指发自深处的怜悯。
life_connection: 对家人的语气比对同事差
一天的耐心用在外面了
睡前后悔自己说话的方式

en.meditation:
The word for tenderhearted literally means having soft insides. It is a physical word — compassion felt in the gut, not decided in the head. And notice the measure Paul gives. Not: forgive as much as they deserve. Not: forgive proportionally. As God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you. That is a very high bar and, oddly, a very freeing one — because it takes the entire question of who deserves what off the table before you start.

So here is tonight's honest question. Where did your voice go hard today, and who received it — and was it the person who had actually earned it?
en.action_step: Think of how you spoke at home today. Pick one moment, and decide how you will say it differently tomorrow.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, my voice went hard today with someone who did not deserve the worst of me, and I know exactly when. Soften what has gone hard in me. Let me be kind at home tomorrow — not because they earned it, but because that is not how You have ever measured it with me. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.

traditional.text: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.

modern.text: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.

exegesis.context_note: The very next verse says God counts the stars and names each one — the psalm deliberately puts these side by side. Binding up is slow, physical, unglamorous work: not a word spoken over a wound but a dressing wrapped around it, and changed again tomorrow.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 bindeth up 与 NIV 的 binds up 同译一个「包扎」的动词;和合本作「裹好他们的伤处」,意象一致。

en.meditation:
Read what comes immediately after this verse: he counts the stars and calls them all by name. The psalm puts those two side by side on purpose.

And notice the second verb. Not heals and moves on — binds up. Bandaging is slow, close work. It gets done again the next day, and the day after. Whatever broke in you is not being spoken over from a distance. It is being dressed!
en.action_step: Name the wound honestly tonight. Do not ask for it to be over. Just let it be tended.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, this has not healed yet, and people have started expecting it to have. Thank You that binding up is slow work and You are not hurrying me. Tend it again tonight. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful.

traditional.text: Continue in prayer, and watch in the same with thanksgiving;

modern.text: Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful.

exegesis.context_note: Three instructions in one short line. Proskartereō means to stick close and not be moved off. 'Watch' is the word for staying awake on guard duty — here, watching for the answer. Thanksgiving is placed alongside both, as the posture the other two are done in.
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 continue 与 NIV 的 devote yourselves 同译 proskartereō「持续黏着」;和合本作「恒切祷告」。

en.meditation:
Three things in one line: keep at it, stay awake, be thankful.

As Christians we are usually fine with the first and quietly skip the second. Watching means looking out for the answer — and if we never look, prayer becomes a habit of asking rather than a conversation. Half the reason God seems silent is that we asked in March and stopped watching by April.
en.action_step: Look back at one thing you prayed about months ago. Ask whether anything happened that you never noticed.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, I ask and then stop looking, and then tell myself You did not answer. Keep me at it tonight, and keep my eyes open. Show me one thing You already did that I walked straight past. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.niv_primary: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for a time of adversity.

traditional.text: A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

modern.text: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for a time of adversity.

exegesis.context_note: The Hebrew is compact: a friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity. Proverbs is not sentimental about relationships — it is observing which ones hold under load. 'At all times' includes the inconvenient ones, which is the whole point of the line.
key_themes: 被陪伴过的人才会陪伴
exegesis.version_note: KJV 的 born for adversity 与 NIV 的 born for a time of adversity 同源;希伯来原文简练,意为「为患难而生」。
life_connection: 生病或变故时谁留下了

en.meditation:
The year everything came apart, most people were kind for about three weeks. That is not a complaint; three weeks is what most of us have to give, and I have been the three-week friend to other people plenty of times. What I remember is the two who were still there in month seven, when there was nothing new to say and nothing left to fix. One of them was family and had no particular reason to like me. She came anyway.

This proverb is not sentimental. It is an observation about which relationships hold under load. At all times means the inconvenient ones. I know now what that costs, because someone paid it for me.
en.action_step: Think of someone in month seven of something hard. Contact them tomorrow, with nothing useful to offer.

prayer.en: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the people who stayed past the point where it was interesting to stay. I know what that cost them now. Make me one of those for somebody else, and bring to mind tonight the person who is in the quiet part of a hard year. In Jesus' name, amen.
